data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["The panel is an active agent attempting to recover information, whereas the compression analogy is passive.","The checklist may include a 'catch-all' item for holistic impression, violating the strict dimensional reduction assumption."],"overturn_conditions":["The panel is allowed to return 'uncertain' rather than being forced to a classification, mitigating the flattening.","The task is strictly low-dimensional, so no information is lost."],"shared_structure":["Loss of information during compression leads to systematic errors on the tails of a distribution.","Aggregate metrics (average reliability) can mask tail-risk failures."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_002","SRC_003"],"transfer_claims":["The panel will show a characteristic 'flattening' of predicted probabilities on outlier cases.","The expert will show higher variance but better calibration on outlier cases.","The distinction between mere compliance and genuine gain is whether the panel's confidence intervals are appropriately wide on outliers."]},"claim":"Against the claim: for tasks with objectively verifiable outcomes, if the outcome space is continuous and the feature space is high-dimensional, the checklist acts as a dimensional reduction that destroys information. The non-expert panel's apparent reliability gain is merely compliance with a low-dimensional summary; a single expert's intuition preserves the high-dimensional information, yielding better calibration on edge cases. Evidence distinguishing mere compliance is the panel's systematic underconfidence on outlier cases.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The checklist is exhaustive and captures the full high-dimensional space (unlikely by definition of a checklist).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The task outcome is determined by a small number of strong features, making the checklist non-lossy.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The expert's intuition also implicitly performs dimensional reduction, matching the checklist's lossiness.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"An explicit checklist forces non-experts to discard features not explicitly listed. For tasks where the outcome is a non-linear function of many weak features, this dimensional reduction is lossy. The panel will exhibit high average reliability by clustering around the low-dimensional mean but will fail systematically on high-dimensional outliers. The expert's intuition, which does not perform this reduction, will be less reliable on average but better calibrated on the tails. The 'reliability gain' is therefore an artifact of central-limit averaging on a low-dimensional projection, not a genuine improvement in judgment capability.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
